166.t: The fight with Leonard Feather at the Village Vanguard
166.s: Carrying ten pounds of marijuana in his hat, he punched Feather on the Vanguard steps, igniting a brawl.
166.q: One night, on my off night, on Monday night we had a jam session down in the Village VANGUARD And I had just flown in from Chicago. I went to Chicago to get some grass. 80.t: Stuff stripped in the snow, the police, and the shaking doctor
80.s: Stuff wandered shirtless at ten below zero snapping his fingers; Autrey called the police, signed him into a hospital and called his sister, and a trembling doctor could not spell Smith.

17.t: Cole's own trio at the Onyx with Guarnieri and D'Amico
17.s: On the CBS staff he led a trio at the Onyx; Sinatra came to listen and punched a man who stood in front of him.
17.ch: Stuff Smith, 52nd Street and session work
17.q: Yeah, mostly, yeah. Of course I worked in the Onyx, there were different groups, Hot Lips Paige, I was there with Hot Lips; then I had a little trio in there, my trio with Hank D'Amico and John Guarnieri. See, then's when I was on staff at CBS.

231.t: New Year's night at Small's Paradise: the ice bowl charge
231.s: Buck, Bubbles and their wives go to Ed Small's Paradise, balk at the $20 charge and prices, and are accused of breaking a bowl.
231.ch: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
231.q: Getting back to a point I'd like you to know about is that when Buck was a little fella he was all right, but when he got to New York he got to foolin' around with the people in Harlem and he got uncontrollable and I couldn't do much with him. I'd leave him go one way and I'd go another.
